paras: The lynching of Thornhill and Fields was the killing of two men accused of horse-stealing, who were taken from the parish jail at Many, Sabine Parish, Louisiana, by armed men on a Thursday night in November 1880 and shot to death. A coroner's jury failed to identify the killers, and the case drew a brief editorial rebuke from Louisiana papers that said such killings were common in the parish.

In October 1880 Michael Morris of Columbus post office, Sabine Parish, advertised a reward for a horse and a mule stolen from his premises, naming two suspects who called themselves Smith and McElroy. The Sabine Index later described Thornhill and Fields as 'the parties whom it is said' had stolen Morris's horse and mule; the coverage does not say whether they were the men named in the notice. Ex-Sheriff Altheus Montgomery, John Dillon of DeSoto Parish and a deputy sheriff brought the two men in, locked together, on a Thursday and lodged them in jail to await a preliminary examination. According to the Calcasieu Echo, they had been brought to Many from the jail at Mansfield.

That night, after only a few hours in jail, the two prisoners were taken out, in the Index's words 'it is said,' by a crowd of armed men. Their bodies were found the next morning about half a mile below town, both shot through the head, while one wire brief said they had been 'riddled with bullets.' No report names the killers, gives their number or describes the race of the victims.
A coroner's jury was empaneled but failed to learn who did the killing and returned a verdict to that effect. No report of arrests, a grand jury inquiry or a trial appears in the coverage.

A Shreveport dispatch headed 'Penalty for Horse-Stealing' carried the news north on 19 November, and short versions ran in crime columns in Minnesota, Tennessee and Ohio, one under the single word 'Lynched.' These briefs called the men 'horse-thieves' or prisoners 'charged with horse-stealing,' and the Mower County Transcript attributed the killing to 'regulators.'

In Louisiana the Sabine Index's local account was reprinted by the Natchitoches People's Vindicator and the Alexandria Louisiana Democrat, set without comment beside news of a cyclone. The Colfax Chronicle, joining the Shreveport Standard, objected to the Index's 'cool account' and called such killings 'a shame and disgrace upon the good people of Sabine.' The Chronicle reported that eight or ten alleged thieves had been killed the same way in Sabine within a few years, but blamed 'a few hotheaded and irresponsible parties' rather than the community.

The Colfax Chronicle dated the killing to the night of 11 November, while the Mower County Transcript gave the 18th. The earlier date fits better with the Shreveport dispatch, which already reported the coroner's finding at 1 a.m. on 19 November, and with the Calcasieu Echo's placing of the killing in the previous week.

accounts.gist: Two men accused of horse-stealing were taken from the Sabine parish jail by armed men after only a few hours in jail and shot to death; the inquest failed to find who did it.

framing.detail: Out-of-state papers ran short briefs in crime columns under heads such as 'Penalty for Horse-Stealing' and 'Lynched.', calling the men 'horse-thieves'.
The Sabine Index reported the killing in the same column as a storm, without comment, hedging the theft and the seizure with 'it is said'.
The Colfax Chronicle, agreeing with the Shreveport Standard, called such lynchings 'a shame and disgrace upon the good people of Sabine' while blaming 'a few hotheaded and irresponsible parties'.

conflicts.note: Both dates were Thursdays, matching the Index's 'Thursday night' (A4). The Shreveport dispatch dated 1 a.m. on 19 November already reported the coroner's finding (A2), which could not have happened by then if the killing took place on the night of the 18th and the bodies were found the next morning; the Echo also placed it 'last week' (A12). The 11 November date is therefore better supported, and the Transcript's '18th' may come from the dispatch date.
The local Index account is the closer source.
